explanations.explanation: That's the number, friend. "In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt," Solomon began to build (1 Kings 6:1). The writer counts all the way back to Egypt, so this building day is hanging on a long, long timeline. Four hundred and eighty years is a LOT of candles on one cake.

Close, but that's not the one the text gives. The Bible says the four hundred and eightieth year after Israel came out of Egypt (1 Kings 6:1). Four hundred and thirty shows up somewhere else in Scripture, and I think that's why it sounds familiar. For this building, the count is 480.

Forty is a famous number in the Bible, so I get the pull. But the text says the four hundred and eightieth year after Israel left Egypt (1 Kings 6:1). That's a whole lot more than forty. Add a zero and then some, and you land on 480.

Not quite, friend. The text says Solomon, Israel's king, began building in the fourth year of his reign (1 Kings 6:1). So he wasn't in a rush on day one. The month was Ziv, the second month, when the work started.

That's right. The Bible says it was "the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, the second month" (1 Kings 6:1). Solomon is Israel's king, and the building began in year four, not year one. Good eye, baker.

explanations.answer: Keep all God's commandments and walk in them
explanations.explanation: Yes! God says, "if you walk in My statutes, carry out My ordinances, and keep all My commandments by walking in them, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David" (1 Kings 6:12). Notice it's about walking, not just knowing. That's the 'if' right there. Then comes the promise.

explanations.answer: Bring a thousand offerings to the new altar
explanations.explanation: That's a big number, and I like the energy. But it's not what God asks here. He says Solomon is to walk in His statutes, carry out His ordinances, and keep all His commandments (1 Kings 6:12). Nothing about a thousand offerings in these words.

explanations.answer: Build the temple bigger than any palace
explanations.explanation: Bigger is not the 'if' here, friend. God says Solomon must "walk in My statutes, carry out My ordinances, and keep all My commandments by walking in them" (1 Kings 6:12). The size of the building isn't what He names. He asks Solomon to walk in what He's said.

explanations.answer: Dwell among them and not abandon them
explanations.explanation: That's it. God says, "I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel" (1 Kings 6:13). Read that slowly. He doesn't say He'll visit. He says He'll dwell among them. I'd frame that line if I had a wall.

explanations.answer: Make them the greatest of all nations
explanations.explanation: Sounds impressive, but that's not what God says here. His promise is, "I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel" (1 Kings 6:13). He's talking about being with them. Being close beats being famous.

explanations.answer: Send them a new prophet every year
explanations.explanation: That would keep the calendar busy, friend. But it isn't in these words. God says, "I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel" (1 Kings 6:13). The promise is His own presence among them.

Yes, sir, yes, ma'am. The text says the temple "was finished in every detail and according to every specification" (1 Kings 6:38). Every detail. Every single one. I can't even finish a batch without a few crumbs left on the counter.

Nope, it's the other way around, friend. The Bible says the temple "was finished in every detail and according to every specification" (1 Kings 6:38). Nothing is left hanging in that line. The work wrapped up in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul.

Right on the money. The foundation went down in Solomon's fourth year, and the temple was finished in the eleventh (1 Kings 6:37-38). The text sums it up: "So he built the temple in seven years." Count it on your fingers if you like. I did.

Thirteen is a bit too long, friend. The text says the foundation was laid in Solomon's fourth year and the temple was finished in his eleventh (1 Kings 6:37-38). That's seven years, and the verse says so outright: "So he built the temple in seven years."

Forty years! That's a long time to wait on a building. But the Bible says the foundation was laid in Solomon's fourth year and the work finished in his eleventh (1 Kings 6:37-38). The verse says, "So he built the temple in seven years."
